Seven should-fix findings remain. (1) The micro-deposit notice says the payment method on file stays in use when nothing is on file. findings.claim: The three simulator forms now share one request key. The page passes a single `<FormKeys />` element object as `formKeys` (page.tsx:66), and the card puts that same object into three ActionForms (payment-method-card.tsx:82, 89, 95). React Flight deduplicates a repeated element object: it renders FormKeys once and serializes the second and third uses as path references to the first. Before this PR each form had its own `<FormKeys />` and so its own randomUUID. I confirmed this with Next 16.4.1's compiled react-server-dom-webpack server (script at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/4b2d015a-84c8-5610-8630-1a03db5b4a46/scratchpad/rsc/t.cjs). FormKeys ran once, and forms 2 and 3 got "$0:props:children:1:props:children:0:props:children:0", the same requestKey input.
findings.scenario: mutation_request is unique on (user_id, request_key) across all routes (apps/web/src/lib/http/invoke.ts:231-236). In test mode an administrator submits 'Add test bank account (ACH)' and, before the redirect re-renders the page (a double submit, a slow network, or a second click), submits 'Add test card' or 'Settle pending test ACH payments'. The second action claims a key that is already used and returns {status:'duplicate'}, so it silently does nothing. That breaks ADR 0017's one-key-per-rendered-form rule. BIL-03's test hides the problem: it passes one static input as formKeys and only counts three name="requestKey" occurrences (billing.test.tsx:36, 140), never checking that the keys differ. The impact is limited to the local simulator; the Stripe path does not use formKeys.
findings.fix: Stop passing one element into several forms. Either make PaymentMethodCard render `<FormKeys />` itself inside each ActionForm (it is already a server component and can import ../form-keys; tests can mock that module), or change the prop to `formKeys: () => ReactNode` and call `{formKeys()}` in each form so each gets a distinct element object. Then make the BIL-03 test pass a factory that returns a different key on each call and assert that the three requestKey values are pairwise distinct.

findings.claim: It is unverified that Stripe accepts clearing a subscription's default with `default_payment_method: ''`, and nothing in CI tests it. In stripe@23.0.0, SubscriptionUpdateParams.default_payment_method is typed as plain `string` (esm/resources/Subscriptions.d.ts:1974), while the neighbouring `default_source` is `Emptyable<string>` (line 1978). The SDK generates Emptyable from the OpenAPI spec wherever '' unsets a field, so the spec does not mark this field as unsettable. '' type-checks only because it is a string. If Stripe answers with its usual "You passed an empty string for 'default_payment_method' ... cannot be unset" invalid_request_error, the call fails. The unit test only checks the recorded arguments on a mock (stripe.test.ts:127-131).
findings.scenario: Every subscription created before this PR used save_default_payment_method 'on_subscription', so it carries the card as its own default. A card customer adds a bank account. In receiveWebhook (apps/worker/src/billing/events.ts:213), customers.update succeeds, then subscriptions.update(sub, {default_payment_method: ''}) throws a BillingProviderError. The webhook returns 5xx and the event is never recorded. Stripe caches the 400 under the idempotency key `default-payment-method:<evt>:subscription:<sub>` and replays it on every retry for 3 days. Meanwhile the page shows the bank account (the customer default) while renewals keep charging the card, which is the exact failure ADR 0073 sets out to remove, and the webhook endpoint keeps failing.
findings.fix: Use an update whose semantics are certain. Set the subscription's default to the new method (`subscriptions.update(id, { default_payment_method: input.paymentMethodRef }, ...)`) and skip subscriptions whose default already equals it, comparing against the string or `.id`. The customer default and the subscription default then always agree, and the same retry and idempotency behavior holds. Adjust the ADR 0073 wording ('nothing else pins one') and BIL-02 to match. If '' is kept instead, record a Stripe test-mode run in the PR showing the update succeeds and that the subscription's `default_payment_method` reads null afterwards, before merge, not only in the post-deploy runbook step.

findings.claim: BIL-04 never exercises what this PR changes, so it would pass unchanged on the base commit. It runs only on the local simulator, and packages/billing/src/local.ts is not in the diff: its setDefaultPaymentMethod sets only customer.defaultPaymentMethod (local.ts:573-581), and the simulator has no subscription-level default. The test also checks that the bank account pays an audit invoice, which always used the customer default. It does not check a subscription renewal or a retry of the subscription's invoice, where ADR 0073 says the bug was. The matrix row's 'a new bank account takes over' therefore holds only for audit invoices, and the stripe.ts change is covered only by the mocked BIL-02 unit test.
findings.scenario: Revert stripe.ts to keep save_default_payment_method 'on_subscription' and drop the clearing loop. BIL-04 still passes, because neither the simulator nor the test models a subscription's own default. The regression this PR exists to prevent, renewals charging the old card, would go uncaught by any db or e2e test.
findings.fix: Either model the subscription-level default in LocalBillingProvider (save it on the subscription when the first invoice is paid under 'on_subscription', make attempt() prefer it over the customer's, and clear or replace it in setDefaultPaymentMethod as stripe.ts does), or narrow BIL-04's matrix wording to audit invoices. In either case, extend BIL-04: after adding the bank account, `advance()` the simulator past the annual period (or retry the subscription invoice) and assert that the renewal invoice has paymentMethodKind 'us_bank_account'. Confirm the test fails without the fix.

findings.claim: The verification notice always reads 'Stripe sends a small deposit ... enter its code', but setupOutcome accepts any verify_with_microdeposits next action. Stripe also uses microdeposit_type 'amounts' (two deposits whose amounts the customer enters), and the test fixture even carries microdeposit_type.
findings.scenario: A bank Stripe verifies by amounts shows a notice telling the administrator to look for one deposit and a code. They see two deposits and no code, and may abandon verification.
findings.fix: Carry microdeposits.microdeposit_type in the verification_pending outcome. Render 'enter its code' for 'descriptor_code' and 'enter the two amounts' for 'amounts', and add both cases to the BIL-01 test.

1.summary: Overall the PR is sound on authorization, PHI, CSRF, the browser bundle and the verification-link href. It needs three should-fixes before merge and has one nit. S1: the payment-method-card refactor passes one `<FormKeys />` element into three simulator forms. React Flight renders a repeated element once, which I confirmed with Next 16.4.1's flight server, so all three forms now share one request key and a second submit before the redirect comes back as 'duplicate'. S2: the subscription-clearing loop sends `default_payment_method: ''`. stripe@23 types that field as plain string, not Emptyable, and nothing proves Stripe accepts the clear. If Stripe refuses it, every setup_intent.succeeded for a pre-existing subscription would make the webhook fail on every retry, and the renewal would keep charging the card. Setting the subscription's default to the new method avoids the question. S3: BIL-04 runs on the unchanged simulator, which has no subscription-level default, and checks an audit invoice rather than a renewal, so it would pass without the fix. Nit S4: the micro-deposit notice copy is wrong for Stripe's 'amounts' verification. All tests pass (54 unit, 7 db).
